# Adversarial verification of issue #931 — the collision disclosure

**Claim under test (verbatim):** *When the sink writes its archive to a suffixed destination because the
unsuffixed one already existed, the committed record names that fact — discoverable from the committed
record alone, without inspecting the filesystem.*

**Surface:** `scripts/kaola-workflow-sink-merge.js` + the codex / gitlab / gitea copies; test artifact
`scripts/test-sink-merge.js`. Baseline `68cb48f4`.

**Analytical result: REFUTED.** One concrete counterexample, driven end to end on three editions
(canonical, gitlab, gitea; codex is byte-identical to canonical): the disclosure fires on runs where **no
collision happened**, writing a false statement into the committed and pushed record — the exact harm
class #931 exists to remove.

Confidence: high. R1 was executed, not reasoned, on the shipped modules, and the causal chain was
measured with an `fs` call trace rather than inferred.

## R1 — CONFIRMED, BLOCKING. The disclosure fires when nothing collided

### The counterexample

A sole-archiver sink on a repo with **no pre-existing archive of any kind** commits this into
`finalization-summary.md`, on the default branch, and pushes it:

```
archive_collision: kaola-workflow/archive/issue-93311/ already existed, so this run was archived to
kaola-workflow/archive/issue-93311.archived-2026-08-03T17-57-20-648Z/ instead. The pre-existing directory
was left exactly where it was — a SECOND archive standing for this project, no part of this one. What it
holds, and whether the repository tracks it at all, is not recorded here: read it before treating this
archive as the run's whole record.
```

Every load-bearing clause is false:

- `kaola-workflow/archive/issue-93311/` did **not** already exist. The sink created it, in this same
  process, minutes earlier.
- It is not "a SECOND archive standing for this project". It held one file: this run's own
  `.cache/sink-receipt.json` transaction journal.
- It was not "left exactly where it was". On terminal success the sink deletes it, so the committed
  record tells a reader to go read a directory that is not there.

### The causal chain, measured

Traced with an `fs` wrapper preloaded into the sink process (`--require`), so the shipped modules were
executed unmodified:

1. `resolveSinkReceiptPath` (canonical `scripts/kaola-workflow-sink-merge.js:1195`, gitlab `:1180`,
   gitea `:1180`) falls through to `return archive;` when main holds no live `kaola-workflow/<project>/`
   at sink start.
2. The first `stepDone` → `writeSinkReceipt` → `mkdirSync(kaola-workflow/archive/<project>/.cache)`
   **creates the plain archive directory** before the finalize step runs. Trace, gitlab run:
   `mkdirSync .../kaola-workflow/archive/issue-93311/.cache at writeSinkReceipt (…sink-merge.js:1176) <- at stepDone (…:1774)`.
3. `archiveProjectDir`'s `if (fs.existsSync(dest)) dest += '.archived-' + …`
   (gitlab `kaola-gitlab-workflow-claim.js:2380`) sees that directory and suffixes the destination.
   Trace: `existsSync=true .../archive/issue-93311 at archiveProjectDir (…claim.js:2380)`.
4. `describeArchiveCollision` sees `archiveDestRel !== plainRel` and `statSync(plain).isDirectory() ===
   true`, and emits the sentence.
5. `disposeSinkJournals` → `pruneSinkArchiveSkeleton` unlinks the journal and `rmdirSync`s both `.cache`
   and `<project>` — after the sentence has been written, staged and committed.

**The codebase already names this trap, in the same file, 1000 lines above the new function.**
`scripts/kaola-workflow-sink-merge.js:1167-1172`:

> `#832: resolveSinkReceiptPath's last fallback returns the ARCHIVE receipt path when main holds no live
> folder, and writeSinkReceipt mkdir -p's it — so the sink itself manufactures a bare
> kaola-workflow/archive/<project>/.cache/ skeleton. That is precisely the residue the incident left on
> main, and an existence-only audit read it as a satisfactory archive.`

`describeArchiveCollision` **is** an existence-only audit (`fs.statSync(...).isDirectory()`). It is a
repeat of #832's defect class in new code.

### Reproduction (all measured, exit codes are the process's own)

Driver: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ylpromax5-Workspace-Kaola-Workflow/b816f7ad-2ce3-40e4-b822-dbb4f0063263/scratchpad/drive-collision.js`
(read-only w.r.t. the repo; every fixture is a fresh `mkdtemp`, and it runs against a `tar`-copied mirror
of the working tree at `…/scratchpad/mirror`). It builds the sole-archiver posture — run folder committed
on the feature branch, sink invoked from main — and drives each port's own CLI with its own mock hook
(`KAOLA_GLAB_MOCK_SCRIPT` / `KAOLA_TEA_MOCK_SCRIPT`, and a `gh` PATH shim for canonical).

| edition | mode | live folder on main at start | `archive_dest` | `archive_collision` emitted | prior dir on disk after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| canonical | control (no prior archive) | ABSENT | `…issue-93310.archived-…` | **yes — FALSE** | yes (journal skeleton, run refused at closure before prune) |
| gitlab | control (no prior archive) | ABSENT | `…issue-93311.archived-…` | **yes — FALSE** | **no — pruned** |
| gitea | control (no prior archive) | ABSENT | `…issue-93312.archived-…` | **yes — FALSE** | **no — pruned** |
| gitlab | n3clone (no prior archive, empty untracked `.cache/`) | PRESENT | `kaola-workflow/archive/issue-93341` | no (correct) | n/a |
| canonical/gitlab/gitea | collision (real untracked prior archive planted) | ABSENT | suffixed | yes — TRUE | yes |

Surviving fixture for inspection (canonical, refusal left the skeleton in place so the falsehood is
visible side by side with the record that asserts it):
`/var/folders/j6/8368yp9j35597_g9_f148lz00000gn/T/kw-adv931-github-0GV2Tc` —
`kaola-workflow/archive/issue-93310/` contains exactly `.cache/sink-receipt.json`, while
`HEAD:kaola-workflow/archive/issue-93310.archived-…/finalization-summary.md` calls it a second archive.

### Reachability

Not a fixture artifact. The trigger is *main holds no `kaola-workflow/<project>/` at sink start*, which is
the posture `resolveSinkReceiptPath`'s `#832` fallback exists for and which all four suites build
deliberately (`buildSoleArchiverFixture` in `scripts/test-sink-merge.js:250`, `mkSoleFixture901` in both
port suites; `#901-*-e` pins it). The repo's own history carries nine `.archived-` suffixed archives,
including the `issue-929` incident, so suffixed destinations are a live shape here.

The common in-repo posture (live folder present on main, e.g. `kaola-workflow/bundle-930-931/` right now)
does not trigger it — which is why the disclosure looks correct on the paths that were driven.

### What a fix has to distinguish

The sink cannot tell a prior archive from its own skeleton by existence alone. Two sound routes:
capture the plain path's existence **before** the first `writeSinkReceipt` (transaction start), or reuse
the predicate the codebase already ships for exactly this discrimination — `pruneSinkArchiveSkeleton`
(`sink-merge.js:1179`): a directory whose only entry is an empty `.cache/` is the sink's own skeleton, not
an archive. Note that route two still mis-fires if the journal is still present at probe time, so the
"before anything was written" capture is the stronger one.

## R2 — CONFIRMED. The (n3) no-fabrication control cannot fail in R1's shape

`scripts/test-sink-merge.js:4311` `testNoCollisionRecordMakesNoCollisionClaim` is the control that exists
to catch a disclosure "printed either way". It passes against R1, and the reason is its fixture, not the
producer.

`buildSoleArchiverFixture` (`:278`) creates `<liveDir>/.cache` and, when `opts.liveCacheFiles` is absent —
which is the case for (n3) — leaves it **empty and untracked**. `git checkout main` (`:292`) removes the
tracked live files but cannot remove a directory holding an untracked child, so
`kaola-workflow/<project>/` survives on main. `resolveSinkReceiptPath` therefore returns the *live* path,
no archive skeleton is manufactured, the destination stays plain, and (n3)'s own precondition
(`committedSuffixedArchiveRel(...) === null`, `:4323`) is satisfied.

Single-axis proof, driven: my `control` and `n3clone` modes differ **only** in whether the live `.cache/`
carries files and is force-added. `control` (tracked `.cache` → whole live tree removed by checkout →
liveDir ABSENT) reproduces R1. `n3clone` (empty untracked `.cache` → liveDir PRESENT) lands at the plain
path with no disclosure. Both were run on gitlab; canonical and gitea reproduce the `control` half.

So the suite's green is real but does not cover the axis: 693 assertions, exit 0, measured in my mirror.
A control for R1 has to drive the sole-archiver posture with the live `.cache/` genuinely gone from main.

## R3 — PLAUSIBLE (reasoned from the code path, not driven). Crash-resume drops the disclosure

`receipt.archive_dest` is set in memory at `sink-merge.js:2233` and only reaches disk at
`stepDone('finalize')` (`:2295`). A process death in that window (SIGKILL, host loss, an EACCES on the
receipt write) leaves a persisted receipt with **no** `archive_dest`, while the archive has already been
renamed to the suffixed destination.

On resume the finalize step re-runs, `archiveProjectDir` returns `{ skipped: 'source-missing' }`
(`kaola-gitlab-workflow-claim.js:2204` and twins — no `dest` field), so `receipt.archive_dest` stays
undefined. Two consequences:

- `describeArchiveCollision(mainRoot, project, undefined)` returns `null` at its first line — the
  disclosure is silently lost for a run that really did collide.
- `resolveRunRecordDir(mainRoot, project, undefined)` (`:107`) then resolves to candidate 2,
  `kaola-workflow/archive/<project>` — **the pre-existing archive** — so `persistSinkFindingsToSummary`
  appends `## Sink Findings` into the very directory the first attempt's sentence promised was "left
  exactly where it was". The second half of that is pre-existing behaviour, not introduced by #931; the
  first half is new and is squarely inside the claim.

Not driven: I could not time a kill into that window cheaply, and hand-building the post-crash state was
out of proportion to the severity. Recorded as reasoned, not measured.

## R4 — CONFIRMED. A comment claim true only of the canonical edition

`kaola-gitlab-workflow-sink-merge.js:97-101` and `kaola-gitea-workflow-sink-merge.js:97-101` both say:

> `recordSinkFinding writes a FINDING line to stderr and a `findings` key onto the envelope, and the
> collision run is pinned to carry neither.`

Canonical's version of the same comment names the pin: `(#700 c)`, which is real
(`scripts/test-sink-merge.js:429` `testCollisionSuffixedArchiveCommittedAndDisposed`, asserting
`!('findings' in out)` at `:447`). The ports' suites carry no such pin — `test-gitlab-sinks.js` and
`test-gitea-sinks.js` contain no collision-run findings assertion; their only `findings` assertions are the
live-folder guard, which *requires* a finding. A reader of the gitlab file who goes looking for the pin the
comment asserts will not find one in that edition.

This is the "prose absolute true only of the root edition" class, and the "specify the result, never the
method" rule: the fact is durable, the mechanism claim rots. The rest of both port comments checks out —
`closure-audit` exists per edition, `archiveProjectDir` is four copies of `claim.js` in four editions, and
the two suffix sites are present in every port's `claim.js`.

## Attacks that did NOT refute the claim

Each of these was run to a result; none broke the claim.

1. **Wiring, not text — the joint the brief called weakest.** `describeArchiveCollision` is genuinely
   called on the live sink path in gitlab and gitea, and its return value genuinely reaches the committed
   summary. Driven end to end through each port's own CLI with a real prior archive planted: both emit the
   correct disclosure, at `status: sinked`, exit 0, readable out of `git show HEAD:…`. Canonical the same.
   Codex is byte-identical to canonical (`bc6b84907c9296975a76…`, both files). The static sweep's stated
   blind spot is real but is not hiding a miswiring.

2. **(n4) vacuous-green.** All three derived fragments (`archive_collision: `,
   ` already existed, so this run was archived to `, `The pre-existing directory was left exactly where it
   was — a SECOND archive standing for this `) are absent at HEAD from every swept file: all four
   `*sink-merge.js`, all four `*claim.js`, `kaola-workflow-adaptive-schema.js`,
   `kaola-workflow-closure-contract.js` — 0 occurrences each, `git show HEAD:<path>`. No leg is vacuous.

3. **Idempotency swallowing the disclosure.** `persistSinkFindingsToSummary` has exactly two call sites
   per copy: `:771` in `postMergeCleanup` (the legacy pipeline) and `:2292` in `runSinkTransaction`.
   `main()` routes to one or the other on `--sink` (`:2947`), never both, so no in-run double entry can
   trip the `/^## Sink Findings$/m` early return. Nothing else in the repo writes that header before the
   archive: `cmdFinalize` writes `## Validation` / `## Closure` / `## Attestation`, `sink-pr.js` and
   `gap-sweep.js` operate on the *live* summary, and `persistArchivedPathsToSummary` runs later
   (`archive_commit`, `:2493`). The one surviving hole is R3's crash window.

4. **Does the new line break a reader?** `archiveCitedMissing` driven in process against the three real
   post-fix archives my runs produced, through all four shipped scanners: `[]` in every case — no false
   `archive_summary_citation_missing`. The regex (`closure-audit.js:349`) anchors on a bare `.cache/`
   token; the disclosure is repo-relative and contains none. Of the other readers, `claim.js:2507`
   rewrites only the `READY FOR FINAL GIT GATE` sentinel and runs *before* the disclosure is written;
   `sink-pr.js:247` and `gap-sweep.js:537` read the live folder, never the suffixed archive;
   `adaptive-schema.js:772` is a name-registry row. The ports' `finalValidationPassed`
   (`kaola-gitlab-workflow-sink-merge.js:315`) greps `/blocked|failed/i` over
   `resolveProjectFile`'s live-then-plain-archive path, which never reaches the suffixed destination.

5. **Path-shape and probe attacks on `describeArchiveCollision`.** `receipt.archive_dest` is produced by
   `path.relative(mainRoot, dest).split(path.sep).join('/')` at `:2233`, so it carries no trailing slash
   and no Windows separator; the `replace(/\/+$/, '')` is belt-and-braces. `isSafeName`
   (`scripts/kaola-workflow-active-folders.js:14`) forbids `/`, `\`, NUL, `.` and `..`, and
   `main()` asserts it at `:2937`, so the constructed `plainRel` cannot escape the archive band. A **stray
   regular file** at the plain path does defeat the `isDirectory()` probe — but it never gets that far:
   driven on gitea, preflight refuses first with `sink_blocked`, `foreign_dirt:
   ["kaola-workflow/archive/issue-93322"]`, and no archive happens at all.

6. **Honesty of the sentence.** In the shapes where a real prior archive exists, every clause holds: the
   directory existed, it is still on disk afterwards (verified in all three collision runs), and the
   refusal to claim tracked-ness is honest — no tracked-ness is measured and the sentence says so. It is
   R1 and R3 that make it dishonest, not the wording.

# Round 2 — closure verification of the R1 repair

Same claim, same surface, same discipline: the job was to refute the repair. The tree was settled and
unchanged throughout (`git status --short` identical before and after; no tracked file written).

**Analytical result: REFUTED, narrowly.** R1, R2, R4 and R6 are **closed** — each verified by execution,
and (n5) mutation-proved armed in both directions on all four copies. Two new counterexamples survive,
both low severity: the phantom disclosure returns over one specific `.cache/` residue (R7), and two
user-facing documents state the superseded existence rule the repair replaced (R8). R3 is untouched by
the repair and still stands.

Confidence: high on everything driven; R3 remains reasoned, as before.

## R1 — CLOSED. Driven on the instrument that found it

Re-ran my own driver (rebuilt as `…/scratchpad/drive2.js` against a fresh `tar` copy of the repaired
tree) in the exact posture that produced the phantom: sole-archiver, main holding **no** live
`kaola-workflow/<project>/` at sink start, nothing planted at the plain path.

| edition | prior planted | liveDir at start | dest suffixed | `archive_collision` | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| canonical | none | ABSENT | yes | **no** | correctly silent |
| gitlab | none | ABSENT | yes | **no** | correctly silent |
| gitea | none | ABSENT | yes | **no** | correctly silent |
| canonical | real untracked archive | ABSENT | yes | yes | true positive |
| gitlab | real untracked archive | ABSENT | yes | yes | true positive |
| gitea | real untracked archive | ABSENT | yes | yes | true positive |

The destination is still suffixed on the no-collision runs — the sink still collides with its own
skeleton, which is pre-#931 behaviour — but the record no longer says anything happened. That is the
right split: the disclosure tracks the fact, not the filename. codex is byte-identical to canonical
(`00e19fa62e4088f8…` both files), so its behaviour is canonical's.

## R2 — CLOSED, and the new control is armed rather than merely green

(n5) `assertDisclosureTracksTheCollision931` is a genuine biconditional: one fixture, one axis (`mode`),
both legs, four editions, driven through each port's own mock hook. It asserts its two preconditions
explicitly — that main holds no live folder at sink start, and that the plain path is present iff
`mode === 'collision'` — which is precisely the thing (n3) never checked and which is why (n3) passed
for a reason unrelated to the producer.

Green is not the evidence. Mutation, in two separate scratch mirrors, all four sink copies patched:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| baseline (repaired tree) | **EXIT=0**, 745 assertions |
| `realArchiveAtPlainPath` → `fs.statSync(dir).isDirectory()` (the shipped defect, restored) | **EXIT=1**, `4 failed, 741 passed` — exactly `#931 n5 root/none`, `codex/none`, `gitlab/none`, `gitea/none`, no collateral |
| `realArchiveAtPlainPath` → `return false` | **EXIT=1**, `7 failed, 719 passed` — all four `n5 …/collision` legs plus `n1`, `n2` and `n4` |

Both directions of the biconditional are load-bearing, on every copy. M1 is the decisive one: it
reproduces the exact code I refuted in round 1 and the new control catches it four times over.

Regression: `test-gitlab-sinks.js` EXIT=0, `test-gitea-sinks.js` EXIT=0,
`validate-script-sync.js` EXIT=0 (*4 Oracle Kernel copies identical at HEAD*), `edition-sync.js --check`
EXIT=0 (*committed kernel parity verified at HEAD*), both run in the real repo. No caller of
`describeArchiveCollision` or `realArchiveAtPlainPath` exists outside the four sink modules, so the
signature change reaches nothing else.

## The early-capture route — the implementer's removal was right, and I can now show it rather than accept it

The lead asked me to attack the argument that a capture at transaction start answers too early. It holds,
and it fails for **two** independent reasons, both measured:

1. **A collision the merge brings in.** I built the shape: a real prior archive
   `kaola-workflow/archive/<project>/` committed on the **feature branch only**, absent from main at sink
   start. Driven on gitlab → `status: sinked`, exit 0, destination suffixed, disclosure **emitted**, prior
   archive still on disk. An answer captured before the merge would have said "no prior archive" and lost
   a real disclosure with real evidence behind it. The implementer's stated reason is correct by
   construction, not just plausible.
2. **A resumed run is already poisoned at the earliest possible moment.** My `cache_journal` shape plants a
   *previous* attempt's skeleton (`archive/<project>/.cache/sink-receipt.json`) before the sink starts —
   which is what a crash-resumed transaction genuinely finds. An existence capture taken at the very top
   of the transaction sees a directory and reports a collision; the shipped content predicate returns
   false and stays silent (driven: `disclosed: false`, and the residue is pruned). So the early route is
   not merely early, it is wrong on resume no matter how early it is taken.

The content predicate is correct in both shapes. Removing the capture was the right call.

## R7 — NEW, CONFIRMED, low. The phantom returns over an atomic-writer temp file

`realArchiveAtPlainPath` treats **any** `.cache/` entry outside `SINK_STAGE_SKIP` as evidence that a real
archive stands there. `SINK_STAGE_SKIP` names two basenames; the atomic writer creates a third form.

`adaptiveSchema.writeFileAtomicReplace` (`scripts/kaola-workflow-adaptive-schema.js:448`) writes
`<dir>/.<basename>.<pid>.<ts>.<rand>.tmp` and renames it into place. It unlinks the temp on a caught
error, so only a hard kill — SIGKILL, OOM, power loss — between `openSync` and `renameSync` leaves one
behind. In the #832 posture that directory is `kaola-workflow/archive/<project>/.cache/`.

Driven, `cache_tmp` shape (`.cache/` holding `sink-receipt.json` plus
`.sink-receipt.json.4242.1700000000000.abc123.tmp`), no real archive anywhere:

| edition | dest suffixed | `archive_collision` | plain path afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| gitlab | yes | **emitted — FALSE** | still there, holding two dead journals |
| canonical | yes | **emitted — FALSE** | still there, holding two dead journals |

The committed line tells a reader that a second archive stands for the project and to read it before
treating this one as the whole record. What is there is a stale receipt and a torn temp file.

Worse than a one-off: the residue is **permanent**. `disposeSinkJournals` unlinks only the two known
basenames and `pruneSinkArchiveSkeleton` refuses a non-empty `.cache/`, so nothing removes it, and every
later sink for that project repeats the false disclosure.

Cheap containment, in the same predicate: ignore the atomic writer's own temp form (leading `.`,
trailing `.tmp`) alongside `SINK_STAGE_SKIP` — one rule read from the writer that produces it rather
than a third hand-maintained list.

**On the coupling the lead asked about:** `SINK_STAGE_SKIP` is correct today for the files the sink
*commits*. Enumerated in all four copies, the only files the sink writes into a project `.cache/` are
`sink-receipt.json` (`:1178`, `:1180`, `:2284`) and `sink-fallback.json` (`:853-854`, `:1179`, `:1181`) —
exactly the set, and the set is read rather than restated, so the two uses cannot drift. The day a third
journal is added, the failure is silent and in the over-report direction: the new journal is not skipped,
the skeleton reads as a real archive, and R1 comes back. R7 is that failure arriving early, by a
different door.

## R8 — NEW, CONFIRMED, low. Two user-facing documents state the rule the repair replaced

`CHANGELOG.md` (#931 entry): *"written only when the plain path is still present"*.
`docs/api.md`: *"the line is written **only** when the plain path is still present on disk"*.

That is the pre-repair existence rule — the one that produced R1. Under the shipped code the plain path
being present is explicitly **not** sufficient: a plain path holding only the sink's own transaction
journal is present on disk and deliberately produces no line, which is the whole of the repair. A reader
diagnosing a missing `archive_collision:` against either document would conclude the code is broken.

It is also the `specify the result, never the method` trap named in `docs/conventions.md`: both sentences
would have stayed true if they had said *when a real archive was already standing there* instead of
naming the probe. `docs/workflow-state-contract.md` is unaffected — its #931-adjacent text makes no
mechanism claim.

## R3 — unchanged by the repair

`describeArchiveCollision` still returns `null` on its first clause when `archiveDestRel` is falsy, and
`receipt.archive_dest` still reaches disk only at `stepDone('finalize')` (`sink-merge.js:2336`), after the
rename at `:2233`. A crash in that window still leaves a resumed finalize with no destination, so the
disclosure is dropped for a run that really did collide, and `resolveRunRecordDir(…, undefined)` still
resolves to the pre-existing archive. Still reasoned, not driven; recorded so it is not lost.

## Attacks that did NOT refute the repair

All driven; each returned a result.

- **`emptydir`** — a bare empty directory at the plain path: silent, and pruned by the run, so nothing is
  left unexplained and no evidence was ever there. Correct.
- **`cache_empty`** — a prior directory holding only an empty `.cache/` (the shape a completed disposal
  leaves): silent, pruned. Correct — it archives nothing.
- **`cache_journal`** — a *previous attempt's* skeleton, the crash-resume shape: silent, pruned. This is
  the case an existence probe cannot get right at any point in the transaction.
- **`cache_fallback`** — `.cache/` holding only `sink-fallback.json`: silent, pruned. Consistent, since
  that file is a journal `disposeSinkJournals` removes and staging excludes; no evidence is lost.
- **`cache_mixed`** — `.cache/` holding a stale journal **plus** one real evidence file: **discloses**, and
  the directory survives. Correct, and it is the boundary that matters most: one surviving evidence file
  is enough to make the archive real.
- **`plainfile`** — a stray regular file at the plain path: preflight refuses first
  (`sink_blocked`, `foreign_dirt: ["kaola-workflow/archive/<project>"]`), no archive happens. Unreachable.
- **`symlink`** — refused at preflight for the same reason in my fixture; `readdirSync` follows a symlink
  anyway, so a link to a real archive would classify as real.
- **`unreadable`** — a real prior archive with the directory mode `000`. The `catch → false` arm in
  `realArchiveAtPlainPath` is a fail-open, but it is **not reachable**: the sink dies far earlier, in its
  own journal writer, with `EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '…/kaola-workflow/archive/<project>/.cache'`
  — exit 1, no envelope, before the merge and long before finalize. That untyped stop is pre-existing
  (`resolveSinkReceiptPath`'s #832 fallback plus `writeSinkReceipt`), predates this bundle and is caused
  by nothing the candidate changed; recorded as an out-of-scope observation, not a finding against #931.
- **Cross-edition parity and blast radius** — canonical/codex byte-identical, both parity checkers green
  at HEAD, no external caller of either changed symbol, both port suites green.

## Method notes (round 2)

Read-only. Every run was against `tar` copies of the working tree under the session scratchpad
(`…/scratchpad/mirror`, `mirror-m1`, `mirror-m3`); the two mutation mirrors are copies, and no repository
file was written. `git checkout --` was never used. Fixtures are fresh `mkdtemp` trees; the driver is
`…/scratchpad/drive2.js`.
